hypotheses.text: dHMN11 is predominantly caused by heterozygous premature termination (nonsense or frameshift) variants in SPTAN1 that cause loss-of-function/haploinsufficiency, presenting as a pure length-dependent lower-limb predominant distal motor neuropathy without prominent upper motor neuron or sensory involvement.
hypotheses.rationale: Reports of dHMN caused by SPTAN1 identify heterozygous nonsense variants in multiple families, contrasting with the dominant-negative in-frame mutations associated with severe early-onset epileptic encephalopathy.

evidence.text: Dong et al. report a novel de novo SPTAN1 nonsense variant causing distal hereditary motor neuropathy (dHMN) in a Chinese family, expanding the genetic spectrum of SPTAN1-related motor neuropathies following previous reports of heterozygous nonsense mutations.

hypotheses.text: Muscle MRI of the lower limbs in dHMN cohorts (including dHMN11) exhibits a length-dependent, distal-to-proximal gradient of fat replacement with an early reticular pattern of fat infiltration that reliably discriminates dHMN from distal myopathies displaying moth-eaten patterns.
hypotheses.rationale: Clinical and electrophysiological overlap between dHMN and distal myopathies often complicates phenotypic classification; imaging biomarkers like reticular fatty infiltration in foot and distal leg muscles provide objective discriminator metrics.

evidence.text: In a cohort comparing 31 dHMN patients against 78 distal myopathy patients, a distal-to-proximal gradient of fat infiltration, extensive foot muscle involvement, and an early reticular pattern of fat infiltration were exclusive to or significantly more frequent in dHMN, whereas moth-eaten patterns predominated in distal myopathies.

source.quote: A reticular pattern of fat infiltration was exclusive to patients with dHMNs, while the moth-eaten pattern predominated in DMs. Muscle islands were more commonly identified in dHMNs (54.8%) but were also observed in 32% of patients with DMs.

hypotheses.text: SPTAN1-associated dHMN11 presents consistently as a 'classic' length-dependent dHMN phenotype with lower limbs affected first rather than an upper-limb-predominant dHMN (dHMN-V) presentation.
hypotheses.rationale: Classifying dHMN subtypes into upper-limb predominant (e.g. BSCL2, GARS) versus classic length-dependent forms helps refine phenotype algorithms.

evidence.text: Classification tables classify SPTAN1 autosomal dominant distal hereditary motor neuropathy under the 'Classic dHMN phenotype' category rather than dHMN upper-limb predominant forms.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact numerators and denominators for pes cavus, deep tendon reflex changes (e.g., absent ankle jerks vs preserved patellar reflexes), and hand tremor specifically in the index 2019 dHMN11 pedigree (Syding et al. or similar) and the 2021 Chinese family reported by Dong et al.?
new_directions.rationale: Full text extraction of the primary clinical descriptions in Dong et al. (2021) and the original 2019 report is required to provide exact per-sign frequencies (numerators/denominators) for clinical discrimination.

new_directions.question_text: Do any reported individuals with SPTAN1-dHMN11 display subclinical myopathic EMG features or elevated serum creatine kinase, bridging neuropathic and myopathic features as suggested by Laurini et al. (2026)?
new_directions.rationale: Laurini et al. categorize SPTAN1 under genes with evidence of both neuropathic and myopathic phenotypes; determining whether muscle pathology or CK elevation occurs in dHMN11 patients would clarify whether it is purely motor neuropathic.
